items.title: Cloud Platform and Infrastructure Account Ownership
items.description: The customer has not specified target cloud account ownership or whether existing AWS, Azure, or GCP subscriptions exist in the EU region.

items.title: Preferred Cloud Provider and Subscription Ownership
items.description: Does Arbormill have an existing EU cloud subscription (AWS, Azure, or GCP) to host this solution, or should the proposal include a turnkey managed cloud deployment?
items.why_it_matters: Determines deployment architecture, enterprise model access, infrastructure cost models, and procurement dependencies.

items.title: Hosting in Customer-Owned AWS or Azure EU Region
items.description: The solution will be deployed into a customer-provided AWS or Azure EU region account utilizing managed EU-resident LLM endpoints with zero data retention.
items.impact_if_wrong: Infrastructure provisioning will be delayed, and the estimate may omit dedicated hosting infrastructure setup and licensing overhead.

items.title: Draft Generation Latency Target
items.description: Response time and latency thresholds for sidebar draft generation and search retrieval are missing.

items.title: Maximum Acceptable Generation Latency
items.description: What is the maximum acceptable latency for generating a grounded reply draft and displaying citations in the Zendesk sidebar?
items.why_it_matters: Latency requirements dictate model size selection, caching strategies, and streaming UI architecture needed to reduce handle time.

items.title: Sub-4-Second Draft Generation Latency
items.description: The system is budgeted for a p95 response time of under 4.0 seconds for drafted responses with streaming text rendering in the Zendesk sidebar.
items.impact_if_wrong: Under-provisioned models will slow agent handle times, while over-engineering sub-second generation requires costly custom infrastructure.

items.title: Zendesk Extension Architecture and Authentication
items.description: Technical requirements for Zendesk sidebar authentication and extension framework constraints have not been detailed.

items.title: Zendesk App Authentication Protocol
items.description: Will the Zendesk sidebar app authenticate to the backend via standard Zendesk OAuth 2.0 or an existing enterprise IdP (e.g., Okta/Entra ID)?
items.why_it_matters: Directly impacts sidebar frontend security implementation, token management, and integration scope.

items.title: Standard Zendesk App Framework with JWT/OAuth2
items.description: The integration assumes a standard Zendesk Apps Framework (ZAF v2) sidebar client authenticating via signed JWT and OAuth 2.0 backend tokens.
items.impact_if_wrong: Custom authentication requirements could extend integration timelines and require custom proxy layers.

items.title: Historical Ticket Metadata and Deprecation Criteria
items.description: The exact criteria and available metadata for filtering out outdated historical tickets and deprecated product procedures are not defined.

items.title: Ticket Deprecation Rules and Quality Indicators
items.description: What specific metadata fields, product version tags, or resolution timestamps should be used to filter or down-rank deprecated historical tickets?
items.why_it_matters: Determines the data ingestion filtering pipeline, indexing metadata schema, and accuracy of similar ticket retrieval.

items.title: Metadata-Driven Cutoff for Ticket Ingestion
items.description: Historical tickets older than 24 months or marked with deprecated product tags will be excluded or down-weighted using Zendesk closed-date and tag metadata.
items.impact_if_wrong: Drafts may reference invalid or outdated troubleshooting procedures, directly impacting handle time and accuracy.

items.title: Source Document Permissions and Access Control
items.description: It is unspecified whether agents have universal read permissions to all indexed Confluence spaces and SharePoint runbooks or if document-level ACLs apply.

items.title: Document Level Access Control Requirements
items.description: Are all indexed Confluence pages, GitHub docs, and SharePoint runbooks universally accessible to all 73 agents, or must per-user ACLs be enforced during search?
items.why_it_matters: Enforcing document-level ACL filtering during retrieval significantly increases vector index complexity and connector requirements.

items.title: Universal Internal Read Permissions for Knowledge Repositories
items.description: All indexed knowledge repositories represent shared internal technical documentation accessible to all licensed support and escalation staff.
items.impact_if_wrong: Requiring dynamic per-agent ACL synchronization will require complex permission indexing and custom connector development.

items.title: Acceptance Criteria for Routing and Evaluation Framework
items.description: Target quantitative acceptance benchmarks for classification accuracy and evaluation test sets have not been specified.

items.title: Quantitative Acceptance Criteria for Release
items.description: What specific accuracy metrics and sample evaluation dataset size are required to formally approve the Q3 2026 production rollout?
items.why_it_matters: Establishes the pass/fail criteria for delivery sign-off and defines the scope of golden dataset creation.

items.title: Evaluation Benchmark Baseline
items.description: Production rollout requires exceeding 85% classification accuracy on routing and 90% grounded correctness on a curated test set of 200 historical tickets.
items.impact_if_wrong: Ambiguous sign-off criteria can lead to delayed production deployment past the Q3 2026 target.
